extracted.intended_audience: students and emerging creatives (design, advertising and related disciplines) preparing entries for the D&AD New Blood Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for students and emerging creatives submitting work to the D&AD New Blood Awards, including what the various Pencil levels represent and the core judging dimensions used to assess entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good idea
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the core judging criteria referenced by D&AD: 'a good idea'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the three judging criteria you must hit to win a Graphite Pencil. Implies originality, strength and conceptual clarity of the core idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well executed
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the core judging criteria referenced by D&AD: 'well executed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the three judging criteria you must hit to win a Graphite Pencil. Refers to the craft, production quality and how effectively the idea is realised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant to the brief
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the core judging criteria referenced by D&AD: 'relevant to the brief'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the three judging criteria you must hit to win a Graphite Pencil. Means the entry should address the specific client/brand brief and its objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphite Pencil qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: To snag a Graphite Pencil, you have to hit the three judging criteria – 'a good idea, well executed, and relevant to the brief.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring note: Graphite denotes work that meets the baseline trio of judging criteria. Use this as the minimum bar for higher awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow Pencil standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&AD Yellow Pencil is for outstanding work that nails the judging criteria and almost certainly causes a pang of jealousy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award-level guidance: Yellow indicates work that goes beyond simply meeting criteria — it's outstanding and highly desirable; typically judged against the same core criteria but at a notably higher level of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Pencil standard (purpose-driven work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&AD White Pencil is for next-level ideas that harness the power of creativity to do good in the world. It can be awarded for any of the briefs, if the work weaves in purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation guidance: White Pencil rewards work that embeds social purpose or positive impact into the creative idea and execution. Eligibility is across briefs if the work meaningfully 'weaves in purpose.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Pencil (best of the best)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow and White winners compete for the Black Pencil — the award that represents the best of the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award-level guidance: Black Pencil is the top prize decided among the highest-ranking Yellow and White winners; carries additional prestige (shared monetary prize noted on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood Pencil (recognition level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wood Pencil: 'If you make it to the D&AD Wood Pencil winners list, then you've fought off some seriously tough competition and are miles ahead of the game.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award-level guidance: Wood denotes meaningful recognition within the awards hierarchy; communicates competitive achievement though below Graphite/Yellow/White/Black in implied prestige.
